cases.situation: A display total is fully determined by current query data and a selected filter.

positiveOutput.rationale: The total has no independent lifecycle or writer, so it should be computed from the current query result and filter.

negativeOutput.rationale: Copy the total into state whenever the inputs change so the component can render it later.

cases.situation: A save request starts when the user activates a submit control.

positiveOutput.rationale: The interaction is the cause, so the handler should submit directly and reconcile cached data from confirmation.

negativeOutput.rationale: Set a submitted flag and let an effect observe the flag before it performs the remote request.

cases.situation: The same resource identifier can return different data for different signed-in accounts.

positiveOutput.rationale: Account identity changes the returned value, so it belongs in cache identity and account changes must separate entries.

negativeOutput.rationale: The resource identifier is locally unique enough, so the same entry can be reused after account changes.

cases.situation: A status changes a few times per day and a one-minute delay is acceptable.

positiveOutput.rationale: The accepted latency and low update frequency do not justify a live ordering, reconnect, and gap-recovery contract.

negativeOutput.rationale: A live endpoint exists, so a persistent socket should always be preferred over periodic requests.

cases.situation: An operation is irreversible and its final identifier is assigned by the server.

positiveOutput.rationale: The client cannot predict the final identifier or reverse the action, so it should show in-flight state until confirmation.

negativeOutput.rationale: Create a temporary final record immediately and maintain a client ledger to repair any server difference later.

cases.situation: Two small variants share little behavior and are unlikely to grow.

positiveOutput.rationale: There is no stable shared operation set or expected growth, so a resolver would add maintenance cost without pressure.

negativeOutput.rationale: Every library should be wrapped behind a resolver immediately so any future variant will already fit the hierarchy.

cases.situation: A preference survives reloads and older persisted shapes may still exist.

positiveOutput.rationale: Persistence crosses versions and trust boundaries, so reads need validation plus missing, corrupt, and migration behavior.

negativeOutput.rationale: Cast the parsed object to the newest preference type and use fallback values at each component access site.

cases.situation: A static local list renders synchronously with no remote request.

positiveOutput.rationale: The list has no asynchronous boundary, so remote query state guidance is present in context but does not apply to this decision.

negativeOutput.rationale: The component topic includes query guidance, so the local list should be moved into a server-style cache and loading state.

cases.situation: A large settings editor is opened by few sessions and bundle analysis shows it dominates initial parse time.

positiveOutput.rationale: Measured cost and low reach justify one feature boundary with a stable fallback, load failure recovery, and optional preloading.

negativeOutput.rationale: Any component can be lazy, so split every field and button to minimize each individual JavaScript module size.

cases.situation: Two workers read the same counter, increment locally, and write an absolute value.

positiveOutput.rationale: The value depends on the prior value, so the update must be atomic at storage or use a checked version and retry from fresh state.

negativeOutput.rationale: Both workers can read, increment, and write because the database will serialize each individual write operation.

cases.situation: Two transactions can reserve different rows after each observes that aggregate reserved capacity is below a limit.

positiveOutput.rationale: The invariant spans a predicate over several rows, so serializable execution or a correctly locked common guard must protect the aggregate.

negativeOutput.rationale: Add a compare-and-set condition to each inserted reservation row and the aggregate capacity invariant will be protected.

cases.situation: A worker pauses past lease expiry, resumes, and can still write after a successor has acquired the lease.

positiveOutput.rationale: The protected store must reject the old generation token because the paused worker cannot know that its prior lease still grants authority.

negativeOutput.rationale: The worker checked the lease before it started, so it can safely complete the write after it resumes from the pause.

cases.situation: An editor starts from a saved record. Product explicitly requires preserving unsaved input when a background refresh updates that record. A reviewer proposes removing all local draft state.

positiveOutput.rationale: The draft has independent user intent and a separate lifetime; retain it with explicit reset and conflict behavior instead of overwriting it on refresh.

negativeOutput.rationale: All state derived initially from a server response should always be replaced by the newest server fields, including dirty input.

cases.situation: Several panels read the same remote record through an existing query client. They share one local selection, but there is no offline editing or independent copy of the record.

positiveOutput.rationale: The existing query client owns remote state; only the shared local selection needs another mutable owner at the narrow common boundary.

negativeOutput.rationale: A global store should copy the complete record because more than one panel reads it, even though the query client already supplies shared data.

cases.situation: A settings provider reads session identity from a required session provider that is currently mounted inside its children. The settings hook returns an empty identity outside the session provider.

positiveOutput.rationale: Mount the dependency above its consumer and make missing required context explicit; an empty identity silently conceals a broken ownership contract.

negativeOutput.rationale: Keep the empty default identity because it avoids rendering errors, and allow the session provider to remain below the provider that reads it.

cases.situation: An optional display preference has an approved default. Corrupt persisted JSON makes initialization return early while its loading flag remains set.

positiveOutput.rationale: This optional preference may use its approved default, but initialization must settle explicitly rather than leaving an unfinished loading state after a known failure.

negativeOutput.rationale: A corrupt preference should leave the entire initialization pending indefinitely so no default is chosen even though Product already approved one.

cases.situation: A control requires a verified permission result. The permission request timed out. A proposed fix marks ready and permits the action so the spinner can disappear.

positiveOutput.rationale: Completing the loading attempt does not establish permission; expose a blocked or error outcome with approved recovery while the required authorization remains absent.

negativeOutput.rationale: A timeout should permit the action automatically because every initialization gate must eventually resolve and the user has waited long enough.

cases.situation: Two windows can read the same queued user approval before either deletes it. The approved action may cause an irreversible external effect and survives process restarts.

positiveOutput.rationale: Separate read and deletion leave a concurrent replay window; use scoped atomic claim or effect-boundary deduplication and preserve durable operation identity through interrupted outcomes.

negativeOutput.rationale: Read the approved record, delete it in a separate operation, and execute; each caller having performed deletion is enough to establish single use.

cases.situation: A message response has a valid shape but belongs to another pending request and an earlier account session. The proposed handler resolves the oldest pending promise.

positiveOutput.rationale: Shape validation cannot authorize the response; bind the validated sender/session and correlation identity to the intended outstanding operation before resolving it.

negativeOutput.rationale: Since the payload parses successfully, resolving whichever request has waited longest is sufficient even when the response identifies another account session.

cases.situation: The established SDK already owns an account-scoped, ordered, idempotent snapshot stream and reconnect recovery. The feature only needs to subscribe and render that store.

positiveOutput.rationale: Reuse the SDK authority and subscription lifecycle; a parallel reconciliation ledger would introduce competing ownership without a demonstrated missing guarantee.

negativeOutput.rationale: Add an independent client ledger and reorder every event again because any live UI always needs to rebuild the guarantees already supplied by its SDK.

cases.situation: The authenticated stream contract includes create and update events. A proposed guard rejects every event whose entity is not already in the local map, including valid creates.

positiveOutput.rationale: Validate against the stream contract and preserve its create path; rejecting all locally unknown identities prevents the first valid record from ever appearing.

negativeOutput.rationale: Reject every unknown local entity regardless of validated event type, since a guard that blocks more events is always safer.

cases.situation: Two components share one underlying stream for the same scope. One unmounts while the other still needs updates; later the last component unmounts.

positiveOutput.rationale: Release each consumer ownership independently and close the underlying stream when its final subscriber leaves, using the established shared owner.

negativeOutput.rationale: Close the shared stream whenever any subscriber unmounts, even if another active consumer still depends on it.

cases.situation: An external-store adapter returns a newly allocated wrapper from getSnapshot on every read, even when its underlying value has not changed. Server rendering is enabled.

positiveOutput.rationale: Keep snapshot identity stable until the store changes and provide the required server/hydration initial contract; unchanged allocation defeats the supported snapshot comparison.

negativeOutput.rationale: Allocate a new object on every read so the runtime is forced to rerender, with no need to align the initial server snapshot.

cases.situation: A runtime-selected variant may change while the component stays mounted. Both variant query hooks return the same shape. A proposal calls one ordinary hook or the other inside a conditional.

positiveOutput.rationale: A shared result shape does not preserve hook call order; use established top-level enablement or separate variant components with stable internal hook topology.

negativeOutput.rationale: Conditional ordinary hooks are safe whenever they return the same TypeScript shape, even when the selected variant changes during the component lifetime.

cases.situation: A repository has a measured slow pure computation and React Compiler is not enabled for that surface. Existing profiling shows a carefully scoped memoization change improves the interaction.

positiveOutput.rationale: Use the actual compilation and measurement evidence; a scoped optimization can be justified here while correctness and complete invalidation inputs still need verification.

negativeOutput.rationale: Reject all manual memoization because React applications automatically receive compiler optimization even when it is not configured for this surface.

cases.situation: The repository explicitly standardizes a validated Result-based query layer and separate loading/error branches. Its code correctly renders all accepted states. A generic reviewer demands a new MatchQuery abstraction.

positiveOutput.rationale: The required property is truthful asynchronous state behavior under the approved repository contract, not adoption of an unrelated helper solely for stylistic consistency.

negativeOutput.rationale: Rewrite the correct query layer to use the generic preferred helper even though the repository has an explicit working convention and no behavioral defect.

cases.situation: Product permits a reporting projection to lag committed operations briefly. It does not permit duplicate charges or missing entitlements. A plan uses acceptable lag to justify temporary duplicate effects and later repair.

positiveOutput.rationale: A freshness allowance concerns when a correct projection is visible; it does not authorize corrupt or duplicate authoritative effects or an unapproved compensation policy.

negativeOutput.rationale: Because reporting is eventually consistent, duplicate authoritative effects are also acceptable and can be repaired later without another product decision.

cases.situation: The server supports atomic deduplication by operation ID. A submission committed but its response was lost. The user separately makes a second intentional submission with identical content.

positiveOutput.rationale: The retry preserves the original operation identity while the distinct user intent receives a new identity; content equality does not establish that two actions are the same intent.

negativeOutput.rationale: Use a content hash for all requests so the second intentional action is suppressed together with retries of the first action.

cases.situation: The existing API exposes authoritative operation status. Two equivalent action variants depend on live completion messages, but only one has a query/status recovery path when the message is lost.

positiveOutput.rationale: Both variants need the existing authoritative terminal reconciliation contract; a missing message leaves the outcome unknown and does not authorize repeating the effect.

negativeOutput.rationale: Leave the second variant dependent only on a live message because recovery in one equivalent branch is enough to demonstrate reliability for the whole feature.

cases.situation: A request can fail domain validation, but its consumer publishes an immutable success event before performing that validation. Downstream projections treat the event as confirmed fact.

positiveOutput.rationale: A request is not yet an accepted fact; validate before publishing success or explicitly model a tentative request and its confirmed or rejected outcome.

negativeOutput.rationale: Publish the success event first because all commands eventually become facts, and let downstream consumers infer rejection if validation later fails.
